newsitem.title: USA: Sundstrand aerospace boosts sales outlook.
newsitem.headline: Sundstrand aerospace boosts sales outlook.

text.p: Sundstrand Corp said Friday an improved outlook for its aerospace business prompted the company to raise its expectations for sales growth in 1997.
The company said Friday it expects sales in 1997 to increase between 10 and 15 percent, up from its original projection for 1997 of five to 10 percent sales growth.
"I think the contrast is more our wanting to be careful in anticipating...what we expected 1997 to be like," Robert Jenkins, president and chief executive officer, said in a telephone interview.
"We also wanted to get verification of the production schedules of Airbus (Industrie ) and Boeing (Co) and others in the industry...," Jenkins added.
Earlier, Sundstrand projected earnings for 1997 of between $2.65 and $2.85 a share, up from 1996 earnings before charges of $2.30. Sales in 1996 were $1.52 billion.

Sundstrand said it expects its aerospace orders to be up in the first quarter, following a decline in the fourth quarter. For all of 1996, excluding a large, non-recurring order, 1996 orders increased about 14 percent.
The company said it expects aerospace sales to be up 20 to 25 percent in 1997 and operating profit up 18 to 25 percent.
"We've been broadening our business in aerospace," Jenkins said.
Sundstrand said earlier that it expects its industrial segment sales to grow by up to five percent in 1997 and profits to increase by five to 10 percent.
Its Sullair Europe division will continue to result in an operating loss in 1997, but is expected to break even in 1998.
Jenkins said discussions continue with unions and the French government regarding possible cutbacks in Sullair Europe operations.
